notes: §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR10 sizes the record of a RELEASE, REWRITE or WRITE from data-name-1, else the record, else the fixed part plus the current ODO occurrences, and (Amendment 2) "the output statement is unsuccessful and, except during execution of a RELEASE statement" the I-O status is set (44, §1985:VII.1.3.5); the SD RECORD clause is this clause (§1985:XI.3.2.4 GR2). WRITE and REWRITE conform through FileConnector#Stored (null -> 44): probes WRITE lengths 4/0/21 -> 44 with USE run and nothing stored, 5/20 -> 00, REWRITE 30/2 -> 44, ODO record of 2/3/10 occurrences written at its current size, WRITE before OPEN -> 48. RELEASE does not: SortEmitter#EmitRelease passes the range to CobolSort#ReleaseStatement, which calls SortMergeReleaseError (a no-op with checking off, all a 1985 program has) and then releases the record anyway, so an out-of-range record is sorted where 1985 makes the statement unsuccessful (§1985:III.2 Unsuccessful Execution: "does not result in the execution of all the operations specified by that statement"). Probes: variable length (DEPENDING and ODO), refusal half (lengths below/above range, zero), file states (WRITE unopened, REWRITE after failed REWRITE -> 43), RELEASE out of range. kb/Work PB5124 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read4/rd-05.json).

next.reason: Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993, Errata C250) added the rule's last paragraph: §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR10 "If the number of character positions in the logical record to be written is less than integer-2 or greater than integer-3, the output statement is unsuccessful and, except during execution of a RELEASE statement, the associated I-O status is set to a value indicating the cause of the condition." Items a to c are unchanged and §2023:13.18.43.4 GR13 keeps them, with bytes for character positions (1985 "During the execution of a RELEASE, REWRITE, or WRITE statement, the number of character positions in the record is determined by the following conditions:"; 2023 "During the execution of a RELEASE, REWRITE, or WRITE statement, the number of bytes in the record is determined by the following conditions:", and in both "by the sum of the fixed portion and that portion of the table described by the number of occurrences at the time of execution of the output statement"). The added paragraph is §2023:13.18.43.4 GR14, which states it as exception conditions: "If a REWRITE or WRITE statement is being executed, the EC-I-O-LOGIC-ERROR exception condition is set to exist, and the execution of the REWRITE or WRITE statement is unsuccessful." and "If a RELEASE statement is being executed, the EC-SORT-MERGE-RELEASE exception condition is set to exist and the execution of the RELEASE statement is unsuccessful." For WRITE and REWRITE the effect is the same: the I-O status the 1985 sentence refers to is 44 in both (§1985:VII.1.3.5 "An attempt is made to write or rewrite a record that is larger than the largest or smaller than the smallest record allowed by the RECORD IS VARYING clause of the associated file-name"; §2023:9.1.13.7 GR4 a) "an attempt is made to write or rewrite a record that is larger than the largest or smaller than the smallest record allowed by the RECORD IS VARYING clause of the associated file-name"), and what follows a 4x status is the implementor's in both (§1985:VII.1.3.5 "the implementor determines what action is taken after the execution of any applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure, or if none applies, after completion of the normal input-output control system error processing"; §2023:9.1.13.1 "the implementor determines what action is taken after the execution of any applicable exception processing statement, or if none applies, after completion of the normal input-output control system error processing"). The difference is RELEASE. 1985 says only that the statement is unsuccessful, with no status and no further consequence. 2023 makes it a fatal exception condition (§2023:14.6.13.1.6 "| EC-SORT-MERGE-RELEASE | Fatal | RELEASE record too long or too short |"), so even a program that enables no checking gets a result left to the implementor: §2023:14.6.13.1.3 GR8 "If checking for the exception condition is not enabled, the implementor defines whether or not execution will continue, how it will continue, and how any receiving operands are affected." A result made implementor-defined, and an unsuccessful statement made an exception condition.
